issues.legal_issue: A claimed genuine land sale used to seek a deduction in determining a ceiling holding must be reconsidered where the claimants were not given an opportunity to establish its genuineness.
material_facts: The family’s holding was being determined as of 6 April 1960.
The family claimed a deduction for a sale of 3 acres and 66 cents made on 16 June 1962, asserting that it was genuine.
The land authorities did not allow the claimed deduction, and the High Court found that the claimants had not been given an opportunity to satisfy the authorities that the sale was genuine.
issues.conclusion: The matter was remanded to the Land Tribunal for fresh consideration of the claimed sale and its genuineness.
issues.legal_principle: In this ceiling-determination proceeding, the High Court found a material irregularity because the claimants had not been given an opportunity to establish the genuineness of the sale. The Supreme Court remitted the matter for fresh consideration. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

predicates.ceiling_determination_proceeding: An authority is determining a person's or family's land holding for the purpose of applying a land ceiling.
predicates.claimed_genuine_sale: The claimants rely on a sale as genuine and seek to have it taken into account in determining the holding.
predicates.claimants_denied_opportunity_to_prove_ge: The claimants were not given an opportunity to establish to the relevant authority that the sale was genuine.

issues.definition: When a ceiling-determination proceeding concerns a claimed genuine sale and the claimants were denied an opportunity to prove it, the sale claim is referred for fresh consideration.

issues.legal_issue: A partition made by registered instrument within the statutory transfer window is valid under the special partition provision notwithstanding the general provision that may treat transfers or subdivisions as void.
material_facts: The family effected a partition by registered deed on 29 April 1970, within the period from 15 February 1970 to 2 October 1970 described as a transfer holiday.
The High Court relied on the general provision concerning transfers and subdivisions, but overlooked the special provision for partitions made by registered instrument during that period.

The Supreme Court held that the special provision would prevail over other provisions, including the general provision, if its requirements were met, and directed the Land Tribunal to examine the deed and the relevant dates.
issues.conclusion: The special partition provision prevails over the general transfer-and-subdivision provision where its conditions are satisfied; the matter was remanded for the Land Tribunal to determine whether the partition met those conditions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21A of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, contains a non obstante clause and provides that a qualifying partition effected by registered instrument during the specified period is valid. If the partition falls within Section 21A, that provision prevails over Section 23. The Tribunal must determine whether the deed was registered and the partition was effected within the specified period. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

predicates.ceiling_determination_proceeding: An authority is determining a person's or family's land holding for the purpose of applying a land ceiling.
predicates.partition_effected_by_registered_instrum: The holding or part of it was partitioned by an instrument that was registered.
predicates.partition_made_during_special_transfer_w: The partition was effected during the period in which the special rule treats qualifying registered partitions as valid.

issues.definition: In a ceiling-determination proceeding, a partition made by registered instrument during the special transfer window is valid under the special partition rule.
